research_concepts: sequential suppressor (preceding opponent play type) stability across seasons
shrinkage and reliability of per-cell efficiency deltas
methodological_questions: Does a star's rank-1 sequential suppressor persist across seasons more than chance selection from many play-type candidates would produce?
Can per-cell PPP deltas with n of roughly 20 to 100 possessions distinguish a real suppressor from noise after shrinkage?
Do teammate X->Y sequences show negative premiums that survive placebo, matching and multiplicity control?
How much of any observed stability is produced by regression to the mean from selecting the top cell in season 1?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether a specific opponent play type on the preceding possession suppresses each star's next-possession PPP relative to baseline. Reports PUTBACK as top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345, n=32; C. Holmgren d=-0.222, n=52). Other tops: TRANSITION (A. Davis -0.058), POST_UP (N. Jokic -0.075). Record notes no multiplicity correction, n_after of 32-95 for several PUTBACK cells against thousands of baseline possessions, 30 stars with min n_after=30, and no validation recorded. Mechanism recorded as unclear. Only the retrieved snippet was read; the full record was not opened.

Looked for named star initiators' lineup and forced-play-type suppressors in the possession graph. Cited cells include Jokic vs MIN lineup PPP 0.814, -0.385 (n=59); Curry vs HOU 0.851, -0.358 (n=47); Doncic vs LAC 0.733, -0.396 (n=30); Giannis forced PULL_UP 0.848, -0.540 against preferred DRIVE. Used a min-15 gate on 8 play types and about 84% DEFENSE_LINEUP coverage. Record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

Audit of action_sequences pattern stability over 23 games, 46 team-observations and about 4,700 possessions. Recorded CV=0.612 for action_sequences and stability CV=0.919 (unstable). Tautological keys with stdev=0 and average of 6.9 samples per key. Verdict recorded as failed_gate, with mechanism A_unanswerable. Recommendation was to merge into possession_flow.

Superstar suppression profiles including Q5c sequential triggering. Verdict recorded as 'rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players'. Example: Jokic after opponent POST_UP 1.1271 (-0.0675, SE +/-0.0500, n=480); Curry forced POST_UP -0.209. Record states rank-1 deltas are mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control and an OTHER artifact flagged in the doc.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking the single top preceding-opponent-play-type suppressor per star by PPP delta against baseline, with no multiplicity correction.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as lacking multiplicity correction; several PUTBACK cells rest on n_after of 32-95; no validation recorded; mechanism unclear. The record does not show that the top-ranked cell is stable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Identifying star lineup and forced-play-type suppressors as large negative gaps from a min-15 gate.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as having no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts (PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE flagged).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Stability and non-redundancy audit of action_sequences patterns.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded stability CV=0.919 (unstable), tautological keys, and about 6.9 samples per key; verdict failed_gate with A_unanswerable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Rank-1 suppressor identification for the Q5c sequential-triggering question.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded rank-1 deltas mostly within 1-2 SE, no multiple-comparison control, and an OTHER artifact flagged. Verdict inconclusive, mechanism E_unclear.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work by this team has tried the same kind of question (top sequential suppressor per star) and recorded it as not a hypothesis test or inconclusive, not as a confirmed finding.
The retrieved records report PUTBACK as the most frequent top-ranked preceding-play suppressor in one family (FAM:SF-APPA-050), but with no validation and no multiplicity control.
Earlier per-cell suppressor effects were recorded as mostly within 1-2 SE (FAM:SF-APPM-022), which means individual rank-1 cells were not separable from noise in that work.
Earlier work recorded that star-chain gaps can be artifacts without placebo checks (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
A prior stability audit recorded high instability in a related pattern measure (FAM:SF-CHT-028).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether any star's top suppressor is stable across seasons. No retrieved record reports a season-to-season comparison of the same cell.
Whether teammate X->Y sequences have negative premiums. No retrieved record tests teammate-sequence premiums.
Whether PUTBACK, POST_UP or any other play type is a real causal suppressor, as opposed to a selection or defensive-assignment effect.
Any corrected or validated effect size. Validation is recorded as NOT_RECORDED in all four records.
The full content of FAM:SF-APPA-050, which was cut in the retrieved snippet and not read.
own_inferences: Selecting the top of roughly 8 to 10 candidate play types per star on the same data guarantees a biased top-cell estimate (winner's curse). Season-1 top cells will tend to regress toward the mean in season 2, so high raw stability can appear without any real persistence.

The stability claim is testable only if season-1 selection is kept separate from season-2 evaluation (for example, selecting on 2022-23 and 2023-24, then scoring on 2024-25 with a shrinkage estimator). Using the same season for selection and evaluation is not a valid test.

A stated unit of n=20 per player-season-opponent is far below the per-cell n of 30 to 95 in the retrieved PUTBACK cells. This suggests the study unit and cell definitions differ across records, and the design must fix them before analysis.

Teammate X->Y premiums are more confounded than opponent-preceding effects because teammate sequences share the same lineup, shot quality and usage. A raw premium is unlikely to isolate a teammate interaction without lineup and shot-quality controls.
uncertainties: The data catalog and glossary were not consulted, so exact field definitions, possession counting and partial-season handling (2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial before the stated completion dates) are unverified.
The retrieved records give 'n_after' for PUTBACK cells but do not define how it relates to the stated n=20 unit.
Whether FAM:SF-APPA-050's full text contains a validation or multiplicity analysis that the snippet omits is unknown.
The probability that a top-cell ranking has any real persistence cannot be estimated from these records.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that the same top-suppressor ranking was already run and flagged for missing multiplicity control, placebo checks, validation and power. Those failures mean the question should not be run as posed. The decision moves from a plain test to a restricted, pre-specified test: stability is evaluated only out of sample with shrinkage and placebo cells, and teammate premiums are treated as exploratory until a placebo-controlled design is in place.

blocking_constraints.text: Per-cell n of roughly 20 to 100 possessions (30 to 95 in the cited PUTBACK cells) gives SE around 0.05 or more per cell, which is comparable to the reported effects of about 0.02 to 0.09.
Selecting the top play type per star on the same season inflates the top delta and biases any season-to-season stability estimate toward apparent persistence.
Ranking about 8 to 10 play types per star across roughly 30 stars without correction makes the top cell a near-certain false positive.
Player-season-opponent cells are sparse. Many star-opponent-play combinations will have very few possessions, and teammate X->Y sequences are rarer still.
Earlier star-chain gaps were treated as artifacts without placebo or matching controls, so a placebo-controlled design is required before any sequence premium can be read as real.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work by this team has run closely related analyses: top preceding-play suppressors per star (FAM:SF-APPA-050), lineup and forced-play suppressors with a placebo gap (FAM:SF-CHT-009), a pattern-stability audit that failed the gate (FAM:SF-CHT-028), and rank-1 suppressor profiles judged inconclusive with deltas within 1-2 SE (FAM:SF-APPM-022). None of the retrieved records reports a validated season-to-season stability result or a teammate X->Y premium test. The question is partly addressed in that the top-cell approach has been tried and flagged, but the stability and teammate-premium parts are not answered.

risks.text: Top-cell selection on the same data inflates the rank-1 delta; season-to-season stability will be overstated without out-of-sample selection.
Many play types times many stars with no correction. FAM:SF-APPA-050 and FAM:SF-APPM-022 both record missing multiplicity control.
Per-cell n of tens of possessions gives SEs comparable to the reported deltas (FAM:SF-APPM-022: SE 0.05 vs delta -0.0675).
Teammate X->Y sequences and star-opponent-play cells are sparse; the stated unit of n=20 per player-season-opponent is small.
Season-to-season reliability of per-cell PPP deltas is unknown; FAM:SF-CHT-028 recorded CV=0.919 for a related pattern measure.
No placebo or matching in earlier work (FAM:SF-CHT-009); star-chain gaps later treated as artifacts.
Teammate sequences share lineup, shot quality and usage; opponent defensive assignments and matchups confound preceding-play effects.
Play-type labels and points come from the derived possession graph; labeling errors or derived-label definitions could shift cell membership.
Roster and role changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 data before the completion dates make season-to-season comparison non-stationary.
Partial-possession and matchup minute fields may be incomplete, so the cell denominators are uncertain.

design.estimand: For each star, the season-to-season correlation of the shrunken, out-of-sample top suppressor delta, and the mean teammate X->Y premium relative to a matched placebo distribution.
design.unit: Player-season-opponent-preceding-play cell for the stability question; teammate X->Y ordered pair per lineup-season for the premium question.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 for selection and evaluation; 2025-26 regular season only after its completion date (2026-04-13) for a single held-out evaluation. Playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis. Cells below a pre-set possession floor (for example 30) are dropped, and the floor is reported.
design.power: Simulate before running: with per-cell SE around 0.05, detect a true delta of about 0.1 at 80% power only if the pooled cross-star estimate is used with hierarchical shrinkage. If simulation shows the planned sample cannot reach that power, report the question as underpowered rather than run it.
design.controls: Season-1 selection and season-2 scoring kept separate. Shrinkage toward a league-wide prior by play type. Placebo cells built by matching on opponent lineup, shot distance and usage. Lineup and shot-quality covariates for teammate premiums. Partial-season 2025-26 data excluded before its completion date.
design.falsification: Placebo preceding-play types (for example, a play type chosen at random from the same candidate set) and shuffled season labels. If the top-cell season-to-season correlation under placebo matches the observed value, the stability claim is rejected. Any teammate premium that does not exceed its matched placebo distribution is rejected.
design.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at 0.05 across all star-play-type cells, and a stated family for the teammate premium tests. Top-cell selection is made on training seasons only.
design.decision_rule: Claim stability only if the held-out 2024-25 (or 2025-26) rank-1 delta is significantly below baseline after FDR control and exceeds the matched placebo distribution, and season-to-season correlation of shrunken deltas is positive and above placebo. Claim a teammate negative premium only if it survives matching and FDR control. Otherwise report the result as inconclusive or rejected, not supported.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons, plus 2025-26 regular season only after completion on 2026-04-13. Derived possession graph version and field definitions to be fixed and recorded before analysis. Playoffs excluded from the primary test.

methodological_questions: Is a star's top sequential suppressor stable across seasons?
Do teammate X->Y sequences show large negative premiums, and can they be estimated reliably given sample sizes per player-season-opponent?
What reliability, exposure sparsity, regression-to-the-mean and selection risks affect ranking of suppressors and sequence premiums?
args.query: defensive suppression sequential suppressor stability across seasons; teammate X->Y sequence negative premium; counter strategy best/avoid; player-season-opponent sample size reliability

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Each star's top sequential suppressor is stable across seasons, and some teammate X->Y sequences have large negative premiums.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=20 per player-season-opp; n=20

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
